habitat: Pairs in dry thornveld, especially sandveld, often with Blue Waxbill. They feed on the ground and fly into thickets when disturbed.
summary: A common near-endemic resident. Both sexes have violet ear coverts and red bills, and Newman says they are unmistakable when seen clearly. The tail is long and often looks broad in flight. The immature is duller than the female. The repeated call is tiu-woowee, and there is a buzzy flight call. The page does not spell out the rest of the sex difference. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Blue Waxbill has powder-blue underparts and brown upper parts. Violet-eared Waxbill has violet ear coverts, a red bill and a long tail.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^13=8192 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 4096–16384.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

tail.shape: Long, and often broad-looking in flight.

head.pattern: Duller than the female. No colours were named.
